The AveLang maxpool1d kernel compiles, passes all 5 correctness trials, and runs at **4.81 ms** (mean) on the MI300X, beating the PyTorch reference at 6.79 ms. Output is in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p41/round0/output_model_new.py).

The design uses a grid of `(B×C, 1, 1)` blocks so each block owns one `(batch, feature)` pair, with 256 threads processing output positions round-robin via `al.range(tid, L_out, 256)`. The inner loop walks the 8-element dilated kernel window, loads BF16 input values, promotes to F32 for the max comparison, and tracks the winning BF16 value to avoid a second load. The host wrapper converts input to BF16, launches the kernel, and converts the output back to the original dtype to preserve the reference model's float32 contract.
